summary:
Echoes Beyond Earth turns NASA's retired Moon and Mars hardware into a story children can play.
Tukunjil, a fictional red-panda guide, tells how Surveyor 3 on the Moon and the Opportunity rover on
Mars did their science and then went quiet, using only NASA records. Learners walk Mars in a 3D
game (The Last Light), scan the rover, test how a dust storm cuts sunlight, and answer short quizzes
that explain every answer. Each story fact is listed in a public claim ledger with its NASA source and
what it does not show. Captions, a cartoon voice, keyboard play and camera hand-shape controls let
learners who cannot hear or speak join in. A museum of 24 Moon and Mars machines and 32 NASAimages supports the story. It matters because children mostly hear about active missions, while the
discoveries of these silent machines still shape new ones.
details:
ECHOES BEYOND EARTH

Project Overview, Technology, Innovation & Impact

1. What It Does

Echoes Beyond Earth has three interconnected parts built around one central idea:

“The machines went silent, but the knowledge kept traveling.”

The project helps learners explore the history, science and achievements of retired robotic explorers through interactive storytelling, 3D gaming and a digital space museum.

Part 1: Tukunjil and the Silent Machines (TUKUNJIL)

An English and Bangla bilingual interactive story featuring nine story beats and eight short activities.

  • Introduces Tukunjil, a fictional red panda guide.
  • Follows two historic robotic explorers: Surveyor 3 on the Moon and Opportunity on Mars.
  • Allows players to read, listen and choose answers.
  • Includes a six-question knowledge check before and after the story.
  • Explains every incorrect answer to help learners understand the facts instead of simply showing a wrong mark.

Part 2: The Last Light (/play/game/)

A five-chapter, 3D third-person exploration game set on a reconstructed Mars environment.

Players can:

  • Explore the Martian surface.
  • Scan and investigate rover components.
  • Experience how a dust storm reduces sunlight.
  • Restore a historical mission timeline.
  • Compare two authentic NASA images.

The game transforms space science into an interactive learning experience.

Part 3: Digital Museum of Space Exploration

An interactive museum featuring 24 robotic machines from Moon and Mars missions.

It includes:

  • 24 historical space machines.
  • 32 NASA images.
  • Source records and mission information.
  • An interactive map explorer.
  • A quiz arena to test knowledge.

2. How It Works and Which NASA Data It Uses

Scientific accuracy and transparency are central to Echoes Beyond Earth.

All factual information comes from NASA webpages, images and 3D models listed in the project's NASA Data section.

Claim Ledger

The Tukunjil story contains 19 documented statements, recorded in a Claim Ledger (/tukunjil/ledger/).

Each entry identifies:

  • Whether the statement is a NASA record, team inference or fiction.
  • The original NASA source.
  • The date the team accessed the source.
  • What the evidence demonstrates.
  • What the evidence does not demonstrate.

Example: Opportunity's Final Communication

The project explains an important scientific distinction:

  • PIA22929: The last data Opportunity transmitted to Earth.
  • PIA22930: Two final thumbnail images taken by Opportunity but never transmitted in full.

This teaches learners the difference between the last data sent and the last images taken.

Dust Storm Evidence

The Claim Ledger also records dust-storm measurements from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL).

  • Dust opacity (tau): 10.8
  • Usual comparison value: 0.5

The project does not invent rover power figures when NASA has not provided them.

Evidence Helper

An integrated evidence helper allows users to search the Claim Ledger using keywords.

It provides information from documented records and responds with "Not in my data" when no matching evidence is available.

It is a retrieval-based helper, not a generative AI model.

3. Who It Helps and Its Intended Impact

The project is designed for:

  • School-age learners.
  • Students interested in astronomy and space exploration.
  • Casual space enthusiasts.
  • People who want to learn about historical robotic missions.

Intended Impact

The main goal is to create a personal connection between learners and retired robotic explorers.

It encourages users to understand how earlier space missions contributed to scientific knowledge.

Instead of simply reading information, learners actively:

  • Scan objects.
  • Test scientific concepts.
  • Compare NASA images.
  • Explore mission histories.
  • Answer interactive questions.

Accessibility

The learning experience supports both sound and silent interaction.

  • Every sound has captions.
  • Text narration is optional.
  • Camera-based hand gestures allow users to interact without speaking or typing.

Hand Gesture Controls:

  • One, two or three fingers: Select an answer.
  • Thumb: Confirm a selection.
  • Open hand: Move to the next section.
  • Fist: Go back.

These are game controls, not sign-language recognition.

4. Tools, Languages and Technologies

The project combines modern web development, 3D graphics, browser-based computer vision and NASA's scientific resources.

Technical Quality and Testing

  • 15 automated tests for the Tukunjil module.
  • 66 automated tests across the complete project.
  • An end-to-end browser test runs the story in headless Chrome.
  • English and Bangla language support.
  • A 2D fallback for devices that do not support WebGL.

Privacy is also considered: hand tracking runs inside the player's browser, and camera video does not leave the device.

5. What Makes It Creative and Innovative?

Echoes Beyond Earth combines historical space exploration with interactive learning and evidence-based storytelling.

Its key innovations include:

1. A Unique Storytelling Character

Tukunjil, a fictional red panda, acts as a friendly guide who explains complex space science through cartoon-style narration and captions.

2. Learning Through Exploration

The Last Light transforms historical space missions into a 3D interactive experience where learners investigate, scan, test and compare.

3. Evidence-Based Storytelling

The Claim Ledger makes scientific honesty part of the learning experience by clearly separating NASA records, team interpretations and fictional elements.

4. Inclusive Hand Gesture Interaction

Players can navigate and answer questions using hand gestures, reducing dependence on speaking or typing.

5. Bilingual Space Education

English and Bangla support makes space exploration more accessible to learners from different language backgrounds.

6. What We Considered: Accuracy, Privacy and Accessibility

The team prioritized scientific accuracy over dramatic storytelling.

Scientific Accuracy

The team removed claims that could not be supported by NASA sources, including:

  • Claims about rover computer health based on a single dark photograph.
  • Rover power figures that NASA had not provided.
  • An image being presented as definitive proof of water.

These limitations were documented in the Claim Ledger.

The team also rewrote two original puzzles to ensure that they only presented conclusions supported by NASA's published information.

Privacy

  • The pilot log is anonymous.
  • Pilot data stays on the user's device.
  • No percentage or statistical result is displayed until at least five sessions exist.

Accessibility

  • Captions for every sound.
  • Keyboard-based gameplay.
  • A 2D fallback for devices without WebGL.
  • Dedicated spaces for sign-language interpreter videos.

7. Limitations and Future Improvements

The team openly acknowledges the project's current limitations.

Features Not Yet Completed

  1. BdSL Interpreter Videos: Bangla Sign Language interpreter videos have not yet been added. The video slots are available but currently empty.
  2. Bangla Content Review: The Bangla text still requires review by a fluent science educator.
  3. Device Compatibility Testing: Further testing is required on VR headsets, mobile phones and screen readers.
  4. Classroom Pilot Testing: Classroom pilot sessions have not yet taken place, so there are currently no measured learning outcomes.

Technical and Scientific Limitations

  • The 3D Mars terrain is an artistic reconstruction.
  • Characters such as Tukunjil, EKO and Bhulu are fictional.
  • The dust storm simulation is simplified and does not represent actual NASA telemetry.
  • 21 out of 59 museum source records are marked "Source verification required".
  • Some mission positions on the map are approximate.

These limitations are clearly acknowledged to maintain transparency.

8. Development History and AI Assistance

The original project foundation, including the 3D museum, The Last Light game and mission stories, was started before the event.

Afterward, the team developed and added:

  • The Tukunjil interactive story module.
  • Its automated tests.
  • Supporting documentation in the /docs directory.

AI Assistance: Claude Code was used as an AI-assisted development tool to support the development of the additional modules, testing and documentation.

The project distinguishes between its pre-event foundation and the work added afterward.

Conclusion

Echoes Beyond Earth is more than a space exploration game. It is an interactive educational experience that preserves the scientific legacy of robotic explorers.

By combining NASA data, bilingual storytelling, 3D exploration, accessibility features and transparent scientific evidence, the project helps learners understand not only what these machines discovered, but also why their discoveries continue to matter.

The machines may have gone silent, but their discoveries continue to inspire the next generation.
